assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mixture
items.clue: Two or more substances that are not chemically joined together.

items.label: Methane
items.clue: The first alkane, CH₄; one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: Crude oil is found in rocks. What was crude oil formed from?

options.text: The remains of an ancient biomass consisting mainly of plankton
The remains of dinosaurs and other large animals buried in mud
The remains of ancient forests of land plants buried in swamp
Minerals in the rock that were changed by heat and pressure

questions.explanation: This is exactly what the specification states: crude oil is the remains of an ancient biomass, mainly plankton, buried in mud.

questions.stem: Why is crude oil described as a finite resource?

options.text: New oil is forming at the same rate that we use it
New crude oil forms far more slowly than we use it up
It is only found in a small number of countries on Earth
It is a mixture, so it cannot be put together again

questions.explanation: A finite resource is one being consumed much faster than it is replaced, so supplies will run out.

options.text: A molecule made of hydrogen, carbon and oxygen atoms
Any compound that contains carbon in its molecules
A molecule made of hydrogen and carbon atoms only
Any substance that burns to release energy

questions.explanation: The specification defines hydrocarbons as molecules made up of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

questions.stem: Which statement about crude oil is correct?

options.text: It is one compound with a single fixed formula
It is a compound of carbon and hydrogen only
It is an element, as it comes from the ground
It is a mixture of a great many compounds

questions.explanation: The specification says crude oil is a mixture of a very large number of compounds, most of them hydrocarbons.

questions.stem: What is the general formula for the homologous series of alkanes?

options.text: CₙH₂ₙ — exactly twice as many hydrogens as carbons
CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — twice as many hydrogens as carbons, plus two
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ — twice as many hydrogens as carbon, less two
CₙH₂ₙ₊₁ — twice the number of carbons, and one more

questions.explanation: This is the general formula given in the specification; methane checks it, since 2 × 1 + 2 = 4.

questions.stem: An alkane molecule contains 7 carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula?

options.text: C₇H₉, since 7 + 2 = 9
C₇H₁₅, from CₙH₂ₙ₊₁
C₇H₁₆, using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
C₇H₁₄, using CₙH₂ₙ

questions.explanation: With n = 7 the alkane formula gives 2 × 7 + 2 = 16 hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: What are the first four members of the alkanes, in order?

options.text: Methane, ethene, propene and butene
Methane, ethane, propane, pentane
Methane, ethane, butane, octane
Methane, ethane, propane, butane

questions.explanation: These are the first four alkanes named by the specification, in order of increasing carbon number.

questions.stem: An alkane can be shown as a molecular formula or as a displayed formula. What extra information does the displayed formula give?

options.text: It shows the bonds between the atoms
It shows how many atoms there are of each
It shows the charge on each of the atoms
It shows the mass of each atom present

questions.explanation: A displayed formula shows every atom and every covalent bond, which a molecular formula cannot show.

questions.stem: Ethane has the molecular formula C₂H₆. How many covalent bonds are shown in its displayed formula?

options.text: Eight, a C=C bond plus six C–H bonds
Six, just the six C–H bonds are drawn
Seven, one C–C bond plus six C–H bonds
Fourteen, the bonds counted at each atom

questions.explanation: The two carbon atoms are joined by one bond, and each carbon holds three hydrogen atoms: 1 + 6 = 7.

questions.stem: Which of these substances is an alkane?

options.text: C₅H₁₀ — hydrogen atoms = 2 × 5 exactly
C₅H₁₂O — it has 12 hydrogen atoms
C₄H₈ — it is also a hydrocarbon
C₅H₁₂ — hydrogen atoms = 2 × 5 + 2

questions.explanation: It fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with n = 5, so it is an alkane.
